security_audit.summary: Most Markdown static findings are benign formatting or example text. Confirmed risks remain in hidden-directory skill-discovery examples, the local Graphviz rendering script, and prompt-injection-like test directives.

remediation.suggestion: Move aggressive test prompts into clearly inert fixtures, and avoid all-caps before-any-task directives in loadable skill files.
Require explicit user consent before accessing ~/.claude or ~/.codex paths, or replace them with placeholder workspace paths.

remediation.issue: Bundled script executes Graphviz and writes files
remediation.suggestion: Document that render-graphs.js needs user approval, and constrain input and output paths to approved workspaces.
Keep ethical limits prominent, and warn authors not to use compliance tactics to bypass user intent or safety policies.

content.value_statement: Skill instructions often fail under pressure or remain untested. This skill helps authors write, test, and refine AI skills before deployment.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to create reusable AI skills and when to avoid new skills.
Defines SKILL.md frontmatter, description, naming, structure, and reference-file patterns.
Provides pressure-test methods for checking skill compliance with subagents.
Includes Graphviz conventions and a helper script for rendering dot diagrams.
Summarizes Anthropic skill authoring guidance for concise and testable documentation.
limitations: Does not automatically validate generated skills in the marketplace.
Requires judgment to separate useful persuasion from manipulative instructions.
The bundled rendering script depends on a local Graphviz dot installation.
Some examples reference local Claude or Codex skill directories.

use_cases.title: Draft a New Skill
use_cases.description: Create a concise SKILL.md with clear triggers, structure, examples, and supporting-file boundaries.

use_cases.title: Test Compliance Under Pressure
use_cases.description: Design subagent scenarios that show whether an instruction survives time pressure, authority pressure, and sunk cost.

use_cases.title: Refine Skill Documentation
use_cases.description: Improve naming, descriptions, cross-references, diagrams, and deployment checks for existing AI skills.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Skill Outline
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me outline a new skill for [task]. Include when to use it, when not to use it, key sections, and one example.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Existing Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this SKILL.md for clarity, trigger quality, token efficiency, reference structure, and likely discovery problems.

prompt_templates.title: Design Pressure Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Create three pressure scenarios for this skill. Combine time pressure, authority pressure, sunk cost, and explicit choices.

prompt_templates.title: Harden a Skill After Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Given these failed test transcripts, identify rationalizations, rewrite the weak sections, and define a re-test plan.

output_examples.input: I need a skill for debugging intermittent authentication failures.
output: A focused skill trigger that mentions intermittent failures, authentication flows, logs, and reproduction steps.
A section plan with overview, when to use, diagnostic workflow, examples, and common mistakes.
A short test scenario that checks whether an agent uses the skill before guessing.

output_examples.input: My TDD skill is ignored when the agent is under time pressure.
output: A pressure-test scenario with a forced choice and realistic consequences.
A rationalization table that captures why the agent skipped the rule.
A revised instruction that closes the specific loophole and requires re-testing.

output_examples.input: I want to include flowcharts in a skill.
output: Guidance on using flowcharts only for non-obvious decisions.
A recommendation to keep reference content in tables or lists.
A note that diagram rendering requires local Graphviz support.

best_practices: Run a baseline pressure scenario before writing or changing a discipline skill.
Keep description fields focused on when to use the skill, not the full workflow.
Move long references and scripts into separate files with clear links from SKILL.md.
anti_patterns: Do not create skills for one-off project notes or standard practices.
Do not hide mandatory workflow steps inside broad description text.
Do not include command examples that access hidden home directories without consent.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps authors create, test, and refine AI skills before deployment.

faq.question: Does it write skills automatically?
faq.answer: It provides structure and review guidance. The user still decides the final content.

faq.question: Why does it use TDD language?
faq.answer: It maps test-first development to documentation. Authors verify behavior before trusting a skill.

faq.question: Can it test reference-only skills?
faq.answer: Yes, but the guidance focuses more on discipline skills that agents may rationalize away.

faq.question: Does the graph renderer run automatically?
faq.answer: No. The bundled renderer is a local script that requires explicit execution and Graphviz.

faq.question: Is it suitable for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
